name: MOVEO
description: MOVEO brings together an interdisciplinary consortium of experts in transport engineering, data science, and infrastructure management. Together, they will develop and test cutting-edge tools, including Digital Twins, to model, optimize, and ultimately improve traffic flow across roadways, rail lines, inland waterways, and port systems. At the core of the project are five real-world demonstrators, carefully selected to represent a range of infrastructure types, climate conditions, and stages of their life cycle. These sites will serve as living laboratories where MOVEO's innovations will be deployed, validated, and refined. The insights gained will inform scalable solutions for traffic management across Europe and beyond.

name: DigiFront
fullname: Transnational Collaboration at the Digital Frontier
description: The Transnational Collaboration at the Digital Frontier (in short: Digi Front) is a research project that starts from the premise that public sector digitalization is increasingly driven by transnational collaboration and asks how best practices of digital government travel across national contexts, and what kind of politically and culturally transformative effects this may have on national welfare states? The circulating best practices of digital government have an unacknowledged political character, as the process of public digitalization does not just streamline the welfare state but also fundamentally transforms the internal working of the state as well as the relations to its citizens, the private sector and other countries. An STS-informed study, the project theorises public digitalization as a transnational network of artefacts, expertise, and events and ethnographically follows three countries deeply engaged in knowledge sharing.

name: CULTIGEN
description: The CULTIGEN project aims to develop sustainable strategies to manage tourism flows, prevent overtourism, and align residents' needs with visitors' expectations. By involving both Copenhagen residents and tourists, the project seeks to build a collaborative, inclusive, and sustainable model for tourism management. CULTIGEN is an Innovative Actions project under the European Urban Initiative, running from December 2024 to May 2028 with a total budget of 35 million kroner. CULTIGEN is led by The City of Copenhagen and is realized in collaboration with Aalborg University, the National Museum of Denmark, StoryHunt, We Do Democrazy, and Wonderful Copenhagen.

name: DataTrails
description: DataTrails investigates how data moves through institutional infrastructures and the epistemological consequences of these movements. The project maps the invisible trails left by data as it is collected, processed, and re-used across organizations, asking what gets lost, transformed, or amplified along the way.

name: BodyNet
description: BodyNet explores how people experience and navigate digitally mediated environments through their bodies. Drawing on phenomenology and HCI, the project develops frameworks for understanding embodied agency in hybrid physical-digital spaces, with a focus on accessibility and inclusive design.

name: FabLab+
description: FabLab+ investigates the cultural dimensions of digital fabrication and maker communities. The project studies how values, practices, and knowledge are embedded in fabrication technologies and how open making communities challenge or reproduce existing power structures.

name: SmartMigration
description: SmartMigration examines how digital platforms and algorithmic systems are deployed in migrant integration programmes across Scandinavian municipalities. The project critically analyses the assumptions embedded in these tools and their effects on migrants' agency and sense of belonging.

name: EnergyCommons
description: EnergyCommons studies the governance of community energy projects in Denmark and Germany, examining how digital platforms mediate collective decision-making around shared renewable energy resources and what kinds of democratic participation they enable or foreclose.

name: AIAudit
fullname: Auditing Algorithmic Systems in Public Institutions
description: AIAudit develops methodologies for auditing AI systems deployed in public-sector contexts, combining STS perspectives with technical analysis. The project produces practical audit frameworks and applies them to algorithmic tools used in healthcare and social services.

name: UrbanSense
fullname: Sensing the City — Participatory Urban Data
description: UrbanSense develops participatory methods for urban data collection, working with residents to co-design sensor deployments and data interpretation processes. The project challenges top-down smart city narratives by foregrounding resident knowledge and community priorities.
